content: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shunt infections require prompt and appropriate antimicrobial therapy to address the underlying pathogens. The following are detailed treatment regimens based on the suspected or identified causative organisms: 1. Empiric Antimicrobial Therapy: The preferred regimen includes Vancomycin at a dose of 30–45 mg/kg/day administered intravenously every 8–12 hours. This is combined with one of the following: Cefepime 2 g IV every 8 hours, Ceftazidime 2 g IV every 8 hours, or Meropenem 2 g IV every 8 hours. 2. Pathogen-Directed Antimicrobial Therapy: Enterococcus: The preferred regimen consists of either Penicillin G 4 million units IV every 4 hours or Ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours, combined with Gentamicin at a dose of 1–1.7 mg/kg IV every 8 hours. Gram-Negative Bacilli: The preferred options include: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 12 hours, Cefepime 2 g IV every 12 hours, Meropenem 2 g IV every 8 hours, or Aztreonam 2 g IV every 6 hours. Propionibacterium acnes: The recommended regimen includes either Penicillin G 4 million units IV every 4 hours or Ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours, with or without the addition of Gentamicin at a dose of 1–1.7 mg/kg IV every 8 hours. Staphylococcus, Coagulase-Negative: The preferred treatment is Vancomycin at a dose of 30–45 mg/kg/day IV every 8–12 hours, with or without the addition of Rifampin 600 mg IV or orally every 24 hours. Staphylococcus aureus, Methicillin-Resistant (MRSA): The recommended regimen is Vancomycin at a dose of 30–45 mg/kg/day IV every 8–12 hours, with or without the addition of Rifampin 600 mg IV or orally every 24 hours. Staphylococcus aureus, Methicillin-Susceptible (MSSA): The preferred treatment includes either Nafcillin 2 g IV every 4 hours or Oxacillin 2 g IV every 4 hours, with or without the addition of Rifampin 600 mg IV or orally every 24 hours. Streptococcus agalactiae: The recommended regimen consists of either Penicillin G 4 million units IV every 4 hours or Ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours, combined with Gentamicin at a dose of 1–1.7 mg/kg IV every 8 hours. Fungi: The preferred treatment options include: Amphotericin B at a dose of 0.6–1.0 mg/kg IV every 24 hours, or Liposomal Amphotericin B at a dose of 5 mg/kg/day IV every 24 hours. Each regimen should be tailored to the specific pathogen identified, the patient’s clinical condition, and any relevant antimicrobial susceptibility data.
